SMTO-TSK-0058 — The Agent planned more steps than this task allows

GUID: a2622b0d-c84c-4c06-91f9-9f5821a5b0d6
Slug: dependency-activity-limit
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The Agent planned more steps than this task allows, either at once or over the whole task. SMTO rejected the new plan, so none of its new steps ran. Earlier steps are unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Send a message asking the Agent to continue with fewer steps at a time, for example one part of the job per message. A smaller plan fits within the limit for a single set of linked steps.
  2. If the task has already done a lot of steps, read what it finished, then start the remaining work in a new message. Each task also has a total step limit, and a new task starts with a fresh allowance.
  3. If you manage SMTO and big plans are normal for you, open Agent Checks under the message box and raise Max activities per dependency graph or Max activities per run. These limits apply to new tasks; tasks already started keep the limits they began with.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's next steps start and show results in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to redo finished steps; check their results first so work isn't repeated.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Graph validation rejected the batch because the run's activity count plus the new activities exceeds max_run_activities, or a connected dependency graph (or a single acceptance) exceeds max_graph_activities in the task's dependency-scheduling policy.

What this means

  • Adding activities would exceed max_run_activities, or the proposed graph exceeds max_graph_activities in the selected policy. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Adding activities would exceed max_run_activities, or the proposed graph exceeds max_graph_activities in the selected policy.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare proposed count plus retained activity_count with both policy limits; splitting graphs does not reset the run-wide allowance.

How to fix it

  • Reduce the size of each schedule_activities batch so a connected graph stays within max_graph_activities. If the run-wide max_run_activities allowance is used up, start a new task, raising Max activities per run in Agent Checks first if appropriate; the policy is snapshotted per task and accepted activity history is never erased to free the allowance.
  • Reduce graph scope; if the run-wide allowance is exhausted, review supported policy/task controls without erasing accepted activity history.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Accepted work fits both graph size and total run activity bounds.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
